subject: squirrels
one_liner: A handheld game console for squirrels, with cartridges designed to be buried and then forgotten.
brand_voice_notes: Written like a 1990 console instruction manual that was translated twice and then approved by legal. Calm, procedural, numbered. Treats losing every cartridge as a feature with a forestry angle. Never jokes about squirrels being cute. The customer is an adult rodent with a portfolio of caches and no memory.

hero.h1: Play it. Bury it. Forget where.
hero.sub: Scurry is a handheld console built around the 11-minute attention span of the eastern grey squirrel. Every cartridge is shaped to be cached in topsoil, and 74% are never found again, which our board has approved as a reforestation program.
hero.primary_cta: Pre-order a cartridge you will lose

features.title: Save files you can dig up
features.blurb: Progress is stored on the cartridge. The cartridge is stored about 4 cm underground, somewhere. Your squirrel resumes exactly where it left off, conditional on locating the save.

features.title: Single-player multiplayer
features.blurb: Squirrels do not cooperate, and our netcode respects that. When two Scurry units come within 3 metres, both players enter a chase with no win condition that ends at the nearest trunk.

features.title: Vertical-first controls
features.blurb: The D-pad is rotated 90 degrees because nothing important in a squirrel's life happens horizontally. Up is up the tree. Down is down the tree, head first, at a speed our legal team has asked us to stop filming.

pricing_tiers.name: Scurry Lite
perks: Mono speaker tuned to the alarm chirp

pricing_tiers.name: Scurry Pro
perks: Location tracking, which we switch off in October out of respect

pricing_tiers.name: Scurry Winter Edition
perks: A dedicated account manager who also forgets where things are

testimonials.quote: I own 340 games and can access two of them. That is the best ratio I have had in years.
testimonials.name: Hazel Underbrush
testimonials.title: Senior Cache Officer, Oak #4, Lot Behind the Library

testimonials.quote: Chase mode has no win condition. Neither does my day. Scurry gets that.

demo_screen_concept: The Scurry handheld itself, rendered as a grey plastic device with a working D-pad and A/B buttons (also arrow keys, Enter, Backspace). Its four-shade green LCD shows the Cartridge Library: 10 burial-tracked games filterable by status (In Paw, Buried, Presumed Lost, Now a Tree), each with burial depth, days since cached and a 'you remember where' confidence bar. Pressing A on a cartridge opens a pixel dig-site grid with the last known location and a Dig action with a 26% success rate that updates the cartridge's status.

design_direction.style: 1990 handheld instruction manual, warm plastic daylight mode. The page is staged as the printed manual and retail box for a grey-brick handheld console: matte putty plastic surfaces, a four-shade pea-green LCD, numbered parts diagrams with leader lines, and boxed WARNING notices. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: rhumb lines, cartouches, scale bars, wax seals, acorn marks, dot maps, status-dot lists, terminal panels, name tags, punch cards, thermal tickets, matte dark mode, lime LEDs, conflict markers, gutter stripes, data strips, viewfinder brackets, infrared, thumbnail circles and arrows. Also absent: dark backgrounds, glassmorphism, neon glow, synthwave purple, gradients behind text. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The LCD: recessed panels in four greens (#0F380F, #306230, #8BAC0F, #9BBC0F) with a 2px pixel grid overlay, used for the hero screen, the highlighted pricing tier and every figure readout. (2) The parts diagram: features are presented as numbered callouts (1, 2, 3) joined to the device by thin ink leader lines, like page 4 of a manual. (3) The warning box: a double-ruled black box with a bold triangle glyph, used for the fine print and the pricing footnote. (4) The plum button: the round A-button plum #8E2A5B is rationed to the primary CTA, the highlighted tier and the pre-order counter. Corners 6px on cards, with the device shell using the asymmetric 6px/6px/48px/6px radius of a grey brick handheld. Shadows are a hard 0 3px 0 plastic-dark drop, never blur.
design_direction.archetype: Feature-rich hardware showcase: hero device on the right with copy left, parts-diagram features, testimonials, pricing as retail box variants, manual-style fine print footer.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Hard, stepped motion only. LCD text types in with steps() timing, buttons depress 3px on press with the drop shadow collapsing, the hero LCD cycles a pixel squirrel sprite. No easing curves on the LCD, 120ms ease-out on plastic buttons. Everything static under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Two columns on desktop. Left: small pixel label 'MODEL SQ-01', h1 in Press Start 2P at 30-40px with generous line-height, sub in Nunito 19px, plum CTA plus a ghost 'open the demo' button. Right: the hero photo of a squirrel holding the console, framed in a putty plastic shell with the brick radius and a 'POWER' LED dot. Below the fold a parts diagram SVG with three numbered leader lines.

images.rationale: Hardware-launch style calls for product photography, so the hero gets a squirrel holding the console. Demo skipped: the demo is the console LCD itself, drawn in CSS pixels, nothing photo-shaped. Remaining 3 slots go to testimonial headshots.

items.prompt: Product-launch editorial photograph of an eastern grey squirrel holding a chunky grey plastic handheld console with a cross D-pad and two plum #8E2A5B buttons, seamless putty grey #E4E1D8 studio sweep, soft daylight, subject right of center, 1990 electronics catalog mood. Hard bans: no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens; device screen is plain glowing pea green.
